_comment: Every place in this repo that asserts what the CURRENT version is.
Version strings in prose have gone stale in three consecutive release cycles,
each time because the release PR bumped version.py and pyproject.toml and left
the sentences that quote them behind. CLAUDE.md predicted the failure in
writing -- 'No gate checks version strings' -- and it kept happening anyway.
Hand-checking a list has now failed often enough to stop being the plan.
The distinction that matters, and the reason this is a manifest rather than a
grep: 'X is current' goes stale, 'as of X' does not. README.md's release-history
section names 5.0.4, 5.0.3, 5.0.1 and 5.0.0 and is correct as written forever.
Only a claim about the present belongs here. Each entry's `pattern` must be
anchored on the surrounding prose, not on the version token, so it matches the
claim and nothing else on the page.
`expects` names what the captured value must equal:
nodus_version       __version__ in src/nodus/support/version.py
latest_eval_version the newest docs/evals/vX.Y.Z directory
To add a claim: write the pattern, run `nodus_gate --versions`, and check it
reports the line you meant. A pattern that matches nothing is reported as a
failure, not silently skipped -- a claim site that moved is exactly the thing
this is for.
`scan` drives the second half: a sweep for claim-shaped lines that are NOT
registered here, so a new one cannot hide. That half is advisory.
Retired 2026-08-30: two claims quoted version.py's and pyproject.toml's literal
contents back at the reader from CLAUDE.md. That was a third copy of a fact that
already has two authorities, kept in step by a claim -- while the gate's own
`version files agree` check already compares those two authorities directly. The
restatement was removed rather than re-registered. A claim is worth having when
prose asserts something a reader acts on; it is not worth having to guard a
transcription that did not need to exist.
One ignore entry was dropped 2026-08-30 with the CLAUDE.md trim: it suppressed a
'README.md is current' sentence that the SemVer rewrite deleted. An ignore entry
matching nothing is dead weight, and test_every_ignore_entry_still_matches_something
fails on it -- which is how this was caught. Delete the entry with the line.

_ignore_comment: Lines the sweep flags that are not nodus-lang currency claims. Each needs a
reason. Suppression is per-line (file + substring), never per-file, so a NEW
claim in one of these files is still reported -- which is the point, since the
sweep's first run found a claim CLAUDE.md's hand-maintained list had missed.
Widening the marker list to silence these would have hidden that one too.

ignore.why: Describes a past failure -- the banner that advertised 4.2.0 through the 5.0.0 cycle. Historical, correct as written forever.

Companion-package versions, not nodus-lang's. Drift for those is owned by tools/check_publish_drift.py, which resolves published metadata rather than reading prose. Duplicating it here would give two sources for one fact.
